answer: A timber is the attacker's unit: one false identity. To enter the kernel, the single ledger where identity seals are anchored, a newcomer must burn vault stake, twice the total the vault has already destroyed. So every timber doubles the pile and every extra identity, honest or clone, lifts the next price: N clones cost 2^N-1 units of stake, not N units. The quote reads one global pile, so parallel clones underbid each other and stalling only raises the bill. If the kernel forks or a quote reads a stale pile, the defence breaks.
